entries.claim: The exact shared digital formula supplies w025–w045 and the distinct Amen w046 after resolving $Per Dominum. The source prints Jesum, a comma after Christum, lowercase qui and no comma after Sancti. The r. and R. prefixes are framing, not prayer words.
The pinned file prints the 24-word body and a reference to the shared Per Dominum formula. The latter has a separate exact source use and raw reading span, not inherited body text.

locator.section: RG 505, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ritus servandus V 1–2, XI 1

entries.claim: Postcommunions are recited by the celebrant in the mode, number and order of the opening orations. The cited rules establish audible delivery at low Mass and sung orations at solemn or sung Mass. The separate Amen is supplied by the conclusion sources. These passages do not alone establish its complete performer or participation mapping.

The Father-directed conclusion supplies w025–w045 and the separate Amen at w046. The proper page prints only Per Dominum. The rubric is unaccented and prints tuum, qui. The reader retains declared house accents, tuum: Qui and a terminal Amen period.
The Benziger 1962 Editio iuxta typicam proper page prints the 24-word body and Per Dominum cue, not the full expanded conclusion. The prescribed expansion has a separate source use.
